newsitem.title: THAILAND: Poor Thai export performance disappoints stock market.
newsitem.headline: Poor Thai export performance disappoints stock market.

text.p: The Bank of Thailand (BOT) on Thursday announced lower than expected exports for September that triggered a late heavy sell-off by investors in the Thai stock market.

Central bank spokeswoman and chief economist Kleo-thong Hetrakul said exports fell 9.3 percent year-on-year in September, the fourth consecutive month of decline. Labour-intensive textile and shoe industries posted poor performances.
She said exports in the first nine months of 1996 rose a meagre 0.9 percent year-on-year against about 25 percent growth a year ago.

"The stock market was disappointed by the dismal export figures, the main factor for its plunge in the afternoon (after the central bank announcement)," Chatchai Saelee of Chao Phaya Finance and Securities said.
The composite SET Index closed down 2.17 percent on Thursday, retreating 20.81 points to 938.42.

Kleo-thong projected that exports for the whole of 1996 would be barely higher than 1995, adding that the overall economy should expand close to seven percent this year after 8.6 percent growth in 1995.
"Despite the low export growth, the GDP for all of 1996 will not be lower than six percent but not higher than seven percent. I expect it to be close to seven percent," she said.
Kleo-thong's new GDP forecast was more in line with projections by private economists who mostly put 1996 economic growth at 6.0-6.5 percent.
The central bank in July said it expected the 1996 GDP to grow 7.8 percent.
"The market was not surprised by the new GDP figure, having discounted it earlier," Chatchai said.
The central bank economist told reporters the 1996 current account deficit would likely hover at its 1995 level of 8.1 percent of GDP.
Analysts said the monthly central bank figures gave mixed signals on whether the slowing Thai economy was on a recovery course.
The BOT said outstanding bank credit growth, excluding imported offshore funds, continued a steady downward trend that began late last year.
It said private investment and industrial output indices registered higher year-on-year growth in September, the latest figures available.
